task.title: Reap descendants at the five remaining Setpgid exec sites
task.description:
PR #72 diagnosed the week-long 80%-CPU orphan: Setpgid puts a measured command in its own process group, but the group is signalled only from command.Cancel (context cancellation), so a command that exits normally while leaving a background descendant leaks it deterministically — and fixed it for the shared MeasureCommandOutput path via reapProcessGroup (internal/perf/command.go), which signals the group unconditionally after Run() returns, placed after the duration stamp so the kill is not priced into samples.

The same Setpgid + cancel-only-kill shape survives at five independent exec sites, each carrying the same normally-exiting-descendant hole: cmd/workbook-bench/main.go:713, internal/perf/scenarios.go:1716, internal/perf/storage.go:745, internal/perf/resources.go:111, internal/perf/validation_scenarios.go:249. (Line numbers as of PR #72's merge.)

Acceptance: extract reapProcessGroup into a shared helper (keeping its pid-reuse doc comment, which names and accepts the recycled-group-leader case) and apply it at each site after any duration measurement that site performs; port PR #72's deterministic descendant-reap test shape (TestMeasureCommandReapsDescendantOfCommandThatExits) to at least one representative site; a ps sweep in the tests confirms no busy-loop helpers survive. Known residual to restate, not fix: a SIGKILLed harness still orphans measured trees — nothing runs after SIGKILL.
